Subject: Performance SLO / Private VPC qualification - follow-up

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the SLO / network qualification for ZenMed's private deployment: 

Summary from call:
- Target tail latency: 95th <= 150ms for single-request streaming responses (avg token latency targets discussed).
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~400 QPS peak during business hours, room for 2x burst.
- Concurrent sessions: ~150 concurrent streaming sessions (token-by-token streaming).
- KV/cache warm-up: model cold starts acceptable for <2% of traffic; goal is <50ms additional on warm path.
- Network: private VPC peering or site-to-site VPN with egress rules; need full round-trip latency from your app servers to our inference nodes <= 40ms to meet SLO.

Action items (proposed):
1) ZenMed: share network diagram + estimated egress path and public IP ranges for peering (Priya / NetOps). Also send a recent pcap or traceroute (if available).
2) Redwood: provide a lightweight latency test plan (we can run synthetic RTT / token-latency tests once peering is up).
3) Both: agree on a 2-hour test window next week to run throughput/concurrency ramps.
4) Redwood: attach SLO workbook so you can drop in expected QPS/concurrency numbers (attached).

Attachments: slo-requirements.xlsx (SLO workbook / mutual-action-plan template)

Can you confirm Priya is the right NetOps contact and share the network diagram by EOD Thursday? Happy to schedule the test window for Wed/Thu next week.

Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming Priya is our NetOps lead and I’ve looped her in. A few details from our side: 

- Priya will send the network diagram + current egress IP ranges (we use a pair of NAT gateways in us-west-2) by EOD Thursday.
- Measured internal RTT from app tier to our edge (us-west-2) is typically 8–12ms; to your current demo endpoint (public) it's ~65ms which explains the gap.
- VPN: we prefer site-to-site VPN initially for compliance, then evaluate VPC peering once we have routes validated.
- On concurrency/throughput: 400 QPS peak is correct; we run a large batch job at 0200 local that can spike to 800 QPS for up to 15 minutes — we want graceful handling.

We’ll attach a small pcap and a traceroute to the demo endpoint but those are internal files; Priya will share sanitized traces. Thanks for the workbook — we’ll populate and return.

Alex

Hi Marissa / Jordan / Marcus —

I’m Priya on NetOps. Attached a sanitized network-trace-stub.pcap (lightweight) and a high-level network diagram (will share the detailed diagram once the NDA/secure transfer is set). A few notes from our infra team: 

- We currently terminate outbound at two NAT IPs (x.x.x.x / y.y.y.y in us-west-2). We can do site-to-site VPN (IPsec) with your on-prem endpoint; VPC peering will need routing approval but is possible.
- Egress restrictions: only HTTPS outbound allowed through proxy; we can open specific IP ranges for Redwood.
- Internal latency budget: app -> edge <= 12ms typical, edge -> peering point <= 18ms; total expected app->Redwood <= 35ms once tunneled (subject to VPN overhead).
- For streaming, token latency sensitivity is high; we want to ensure websocket stability and avoid mid-stream retransmits.

Requested from Redwood: a short doc on recommended MTU/path-MSS and any keepalive/idle-timeout recommendations for long-lived streams. Also confirm whether TLS termination is required on our side or handled by Redwood.

Priya
Priya Singh
Network Engineering Lead | ZenMed
priya.singh@zenmed.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Performance SLO / Private VPC qualification - follow-up

Thanks Priya — helpful context. A few clarifications from the Redwood infra side: 

- TLS: Redwood terminates TLS on the inference nodes. For Private/VPC we support mutual TLS if required; if you prefer TLS on your side + an IP allowlist we can accommodate that too. We’ll include an mTLS setup guide.
- MTU/keepalives: recommend MTU 1500 / path-MSS 1460. For long-lived streaming sessions set TCP keepalive to 60s and application-level pings every 30s to avoid idle timeouts on middleboxes.
- Test plan: propose the following window and ramps for the 2-hour test: 
   * 0–10 min: warmup streaming sessions to populate KV cache (50 sessions)
   * 10–40 min: ramp to steady 400 QPS with 120 concurrent streams (sustained)
   * 40–55 min: 1.5x spike (600 QPS) to test buffering/fallbacks
   * 55–70 min: return to 200 QPS to observe recovery
   * 70–90 min: 2x short spike for 15 minutes (800 QPS) to validate burst handling
   * Final 30 min: network go/no-go and collect token-latency histograms and traces.

- Observability: we’ll provide a short tracing hook so your app can include a trace id per session; we ask you to include the trace id in the request header so we can correlate infra metrics.

Next steps: 
1) Priya to share sanitized traces + diagram by EOD Thursday.
2) ZenMed and Redwood agree on a test slot — can you do Thu 11:00–13:00 PT?
3) Marissa / Jordan will push the MTU/mTLS doc and a short test-run checklist by tomorrow morning.

Jordan
